questions.prompt: Name a U.S. state or a country in Africa
questions.note: Any of the 50 states, and any of the 54 UN member countries in Africa, counts.

answers.name: Seychelles
answers.note: Africa’s least populous country, an Indian Ocean archipelago of about 120,000 people.

questions.prompt: Name a country in Europe, North or South America, or Oceania
questions.note: UN member countries that the UN statistical standard (M49) places in Europe, the Americas (including Central America and the Caribbean) or Oceania count. Russia, Turkey, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan and Georgia, which span Europe and Asia, Armenia and Cyprus, which are often counted as European, and Indonesia and Timor-Leste count.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.note: A Pacific nation of 33 atolls and islands, the only country with territory in all four hemispheres.

questions.prompt: Name a city or town in California, Texas or Florida with at least 100,000 residents
questions.note: Every incorporated place in California, Texas or Florida with 100,000 or more residents in the Census Bureau 2023 estimates counts.

answers.name: Miami Gardens
answers.note: A city of about 111,000 people in Florida (Census Bureau 2023 estimate).

questions.prompt: Name someone who served in the U.S. Senate at some point from 1950 through 1969
questions.note: Anyone who served in the U.S. Senate at any time during the 1950s or 1960s (appointed senators included) counts.

answers.name: Harry P. Cain
answers.note: A former mayor of Tacoma, he later served on the Subversive Activities Control Board.

questions.prompt: Name someone who served in the U.S. Senate at some point from 1970 through 1989
questions.note: Anyone who served in the U.S. Senate at any time during the 1970s or 1980s (appointed senators included) counts.

answers.name: Charles Goodell
answers.note: He is the father of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell.

questions.prompt: Name a Speaker of the House or a U.S. Attorney General
questions.note: Anyone who has been Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives or served as Attorney General counts (acting attorneys general not included).

answers.name: William Bradford
answers.note: The second Attorney General, he died in office in 1795 at age 39.

questions.prompt: Name a U.S. vice president or a U.S. Attorney General
questions.note: Any vice president and anyone who has served as Attorney General counts (acting attorneys general not included).

answers.name: John C. Breckinridge
answers.note: At 36 he was the youngest vice president in history and later became a Confederate general and secretary of war.

questions.prompt: Name a U.S. president or a woman who has served as governor of a state
questions.note: Any president, and any woman who has served as a state governor (acting governors included), counts.

answers.name: Dixy Lee Ray
answers.note: A marine biologist and former chair of the Atomic Energy Commission, she was governor of Washington from 1977 to 1981.

questions.prompt: Name a U.S. state capital or a U.S. city with at least 250,000 residents
questions.note: Any of the 50 state capitals, and every incorporated place with 250,000 or more residents in the Census Bureau 2023 estimates, counts.

answers.name: Irving
answers.note: A city of about 254,000 people in Texas (Census Bureau 2023 estimate).

questions.prompt: Name a Speaker of the House or a U.S. Secretary of the Treasury
questions.note: Anyone who has been Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives or served as Secretary of the Treasury counts (acting secretaries not included).

answers.name: James Guthrie
answers.note: Treasury secretary under Franklin Pierce from 1853 to 1857, he later represented Kentucky in the U.S. Senate from 1865 until ill health forced him to resign in 1868.

questions.prompt: Name a First Lady or a woman who has served as governor of a state
questions.note: Any First Lady of the United States (acting First Ladies such as Harriet Lane included), and any woman who has served as a state governor (acting governors included), counts.

answers.name: Nellie Tayloe Ross
answers.note: Nellie Tayloe Ross became governor of Wyoming in January 1925, the first woman to serve as a U.S. state governor.
